task: round 13 skeptic v_hyp_node_count R13NC-5 (start-leaf prune, lp30 mirror)
reason: As a lever for before the deadline, this is refuted on both value and feasibility. The 'post-deadline' filing is right, but the lab number overstates what it is. (1) 44b6 goes 17/0 with 0 matched nodes and dFP -1, so its whole +0.00052 is node-count arithmetic, not proof that the prune picks the right nodes. On 6bba, 20 of the pruned nodes match GT, and the arm loses 8 TP edges (0.4 per matched node). Pooled enrichment r = 0.137 is about 3x the break-even r* of 0.047. It only comes out positive because each start leaf carries at most one edge. (2) Of the pooled +0.00048, about +0.00032 comes from the node term (0.36% x 0.0009). The other ~+0.00016 is net FP/TP edge removal, and that part trusts the edge network's p, which is in-sample on the train clips. That is the edge-filter lesson: +0.016 in the lab, 0 on the LB. Out of sample, more low-p start edges will be real, so the TP loss grows and the enrichment goes up. (3) ORDERING GAP: ncarms2.py ran startleaf on e_ins, AFTER insert35. The only existing prune hook in the kernel (LEAFPRUNE_CALL, between the short-track filter and linefit) runs BEFORE the divinsert cell. A mirror placed there would delete orphan track starts before DaughterNet can attach parents to them, and that interaction was never measured. A hook after the insertion would be new code inside the safetail-gated tail. It was also never measured stacked on lp30 (probe 40, pending). (4) It is the same mechanism class as leaf prune, which tied on the public display twice (P27, P36), and 'leaf prune on x138' is on the closed list. This mirror is half the lab size. (5) Schedule and rules: at 01:15Z the user is asleep and R8 closes at 12:00Z. The pair rule needs every single knob at >= 0.954 and V* at >= 0.955, so the mirror would need its own ladder slot out of the 4 left on 27 Sep (>= 2 are reserved). The expected public move is ~+0.00008, so P(display flip) < 0.05. Its only use is as an unmeasured rider on a combo, which the ladder rule forbids.
fix: Put it on the post-deadline list, low priority, and label it 'in-sample-edge-p dependent'. A future test must (a) apply it at the kernel's real hook, before insertion, or add a hook after insertion and replay that exact code path, (b) measure it stacked on lp30, (c) report the node-term and edge-term halves separately, and (d) judge it on the node term alone, discounting the edge-p half as in-sample. Do not build a patch or dummy, and do not ask the user for an OK before 12:00Z.
realistic_gain: Public ~0 to +0.0001 (display unchanged, P(flip) < 0.05). Private ~0 to +0.0003, with a node-term floor of ~+0.0002 only if out-of-sample enrichment stays below ~0.09. Not worth a ladder slot or a finals risk.
